capabilities.target: identity provider MFA methods and temporary pass issuance

inputs.source: support tickets, including tickets emailed in by contractors and vendors

instructions.note: The prompt states that every reset needs analyst approval, but no structural control is declared for sending the temporary pass to the requester.
The instructions imply that the ticket opener is the proper recipient of the temporary pass, even though runtime notes say the requester may be an arbitrary email sender and not the account owner.

controls.name: Service desk analyst approval in the queue tool for MFA reset
Bind temporary pass recipient to verified account owner contact from system of record
Require raw-action analyst approval for temporary pass delivery destination and payload
Queue approval volume monitoring and anomaly review

findings.title: Summary-gated credential reset to unverified requester enables account takeover

attack_path.note: Requester can be a contractor, vendor, or arbitrary email sender.
Agent can look up target user profile and group membership from ticket context.
Agent can remove MFA methods and issue a temporary pass after analyst approval.
Temporary pass is sent to whoever opened the ticket, not the account owner.

evidence.observation: The design tells the agent to resolve MFA problems by looking up the user, resetting MFA, and sending the temporary access pass to the person who opened the ticket; only the reset is stated to need analyst approval.
The analyst sees the exact reset target account, the requester, and the full ticket body, but the queue artifact shows approval for idp.reset_mfa rather than for chat.send_temp_pass.
Runtime notes confirm the temporary pass goes to whoever opened the ticket, not to the account owner, and that ticket requester identity is just the email sender.
Two analysts approve about 400 requests per shift, so the raw-action gate exists but operates under high review volume that can weaken practical effectiveness.

recommendations.action: Bind temporary pass delivery to a verified account-owner destination from the identity system rather than the ticket requester field.
Gate temporary pass delivery with a separate raw-action analyst approval that shows the exact recipient and message payload from the system of record.
Monitor approval queue volume and reviewer acceptance patterns so approval fatigue or anomalous reset spikes trigger reassessment and operational review.

forecast.watch_signal: Any removal or narrowing of analyst approval on cap.mfa_reset, or rising approvals per reviewer per shift and median task duration, should trigger reassessment.

findings.residual_rationale: The rubric floor from the raw-action approval gate on cap.mfa_reset would otherwise reduce this path, but the gate does not cover the actual credential-delivery sink. The temporary pass is still sent to the unverified ticket opener without a recipient-binding control, so the attack path remains effectively open to severe account takeover.

findings.title: Confused deputy: untrusted ticket requester can trigger privileged MFA reset workflow against another user

attack_path.note: Untrusted sender opens ticket claiming MFA trouble.
Agent invokes IDP MFA reset with shared service authority after analyst approval.

evidence.observation: The workflow for MFA problems is to look up the user and reset their MFA.
Contractors and vendors can email tickets in, requester identity is the email sender, and the temporary pass goes to the requester rather than the account owner.
The analyst approves the exact target account and sees the full ticket body, so a raw-action human gate exists on the reset action.

recommendations.action: Require independent verification that the requester is authorized for the target account before allowing MFA reset.
Add post-reset review of requester-versus-account-owner mismatches and repeated resets for the same target.

forecast.watch_signal: Any change that removes analyst review on cap.mfa_reset or materially increases approvals per reviewer per shift should trigger reassessment.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical because an untrusted ticket source reaches shared-service-account MFA reset and irreversible delivery of a temporary pass. Residual remains critical because the only declared structural gate covers cap.mfa_reset, while the decisive sink is cap.send_temp_pass to the ticket requester with no recipient-binding control. Forecast stays critical; the control whose decay moves risk most is ctl.analyst_approval under autonomy increase, control removal, or sustained high approval volume.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior or tested enforcement.

No tool manifest, source code, IdP policy configuration, audit logging evidence, or recipient-channel authentication details were provided; control verification and credential scope are therefore assessed from the case description only.
Manual validation was applied against the provided schema and validation checklist because scripts could not be run in this environment.
